text:
jordan-pm: Heads-up — AcmeHealth asked for automated recommendations that pick batching/caching/quant profiles per route + eval-triggered alerts. They want a pilot we can ship without changing their model. p99 latency target ~150ms, goal 30% token cost reduction. Can we sketch scope?
maya-eng: short answer: yes, but need constraints. do we want runtime-only recommendations or config + guidance?
simon-ml: runtime-only first. we can suggest a quant profile and batching window, but if they want auto-apply we'll need extra opt-in + safety checks.
linh-ux: UI: needs a simple "Suggested profile" card and an explain link. customers want one-click apply for pilots.
ara-ops: ops considerations: must not break SLA. suggestions must include a fallback to baseline model and traffic split for canary. also audit logs for every auto-change.
carl-cs: AcmeHealth pushed on eval alerts — they want immediate notice when quality drops on a small set of golden prompts. are we planning eval-run frequency?
simon-ml: proposal: run nightly evals on customer-provided prompt set + a lightweight on-write check per rollout (sample 100 requests and compute concordance). trigger thresholds: delta > 3% F1 or >5% semantic drift => alert.
jordan-pm: launch criteria idea: 1) Recommend profiles with measured cost/latency delta on staging 2) Canary auto-apply to 5% traffic + rollback on eval failure 3) UI affordance + audit trail 4) Ops playbook and SLOs documented
maya-eng: implementation notes: need telemetry hooks to report per-route latency distribution, token counts, and cache hit rate. batching suggestion depends on seq length distribution; we should include a recommended batch-size + expected latency vs cost curve.
linh-ux: for the pilot UX, minimal: Suggested profile (batch_size, quant_level, cache_ttl), Expected impact (tokens saved, p99 change), Confidence score, and an "Apply to Canary" button.
ara-ops: also include a forced-disable flag per-tenant and a ttl for auto-runs. make sure KMS keys not exposed in logs.
carl-cs: docs for customers: one-pager on "what changes when you accept a recommendation" and an opt-out process. AcmeHealth legal asked about rollback SLAs.
simon-ml: rough engineering estimate: 3 wks to build offline recommender + simulation harness, 2 wks to integrate runtime telemetry + decision engine, 1 wk for canary plumbing and rollback, 1 wk for UI + docs = ~7 weeks. depends on priorities.
jordan-pm: tradeoffs: fully automated apply reduces friction but increases risk. manual apply increases time-to-value. pilot should default to suggestion + one-click canary.
maya-eng: risk items: quantization may affect output distribution. must gate auto-apply on eval concordance threshold. also watch rare tokenization edge cases. build guardrail tests.
linh-ux: can we prototype the UI with a fake suggestion flow for user testing this week? tiny mock will help acceptance criteria.
simon-ml: yes. I'll generate sample recommendations from the sim harness and push a mock API.
ara-ops: Are we comfortable with a nightly batch evaluation cadence to start? not real-time but quick enough to catch regressions.
carl-cs: customer ask: they'd like a weekly summary email of suggestions + applied changes. add to scope?
jordan-pm: add weekly summary to MVP but make it opt-in. acceptance: AcmeHealth pilot should see at least 15% cost reduction in 4 weeks with no >3% quality regression on golden set.
maya-eng: next steps: 1) sim harness PR by simon 2) telemetry schema doc by me 3) mock UI by linh 4) ops runbook draft by ara. owners listed in thread.
simon-ml: creating branch now. tagging @deploy-bot for canary checklist when ready.
deploy-bot: Deploy checklist created: canary traffic split, rollback hook, alerting. runbook link: https://internal/runbooks/opt-recs-canary
jordan-pm: great. i'll reach out to AcmeHealth to confirm acceptance metrics and golden prompts. thanks team — syncing again next Tue. :thumbsup:
